correctness.rationale: On the quotient by tM a commuting map induces a triangular matrix whose diagonal is the two diagonal constant coefficients. Nilpotence implies they vanish; conversely the resulting square sends M into tM, so iteration gives nilpotence. Dividing the long-block image by t and factoring out the killed top coordinate of the long source gives an ordinary-rank-preserving 2×2 map over R_l with lower-right entry in tR_l, l=m−1. Zero residue lowers l by one without changing the image dimension. A unit residue pivot in rank one leaves a 1×1 Schur complement in tR_l; for each fixed residue the opposite entry is uniform over its residue class, giving q^{3(l−1)} lifts per complement, also when the lower-right entry must vanish mod t. A scalar of ordinary rank r has valuation l−r, giving H_l. The invertible residue count q(q−1)^2 and rank-one count 2q²−q−1 give the stated P; full rank of the reduced map is exactly b_0 c_0 ≠ 0 and gives the product stratum. This holds for l=1 and in characteristic two. Independent literal enumeration of commuting matrices over GF(2), testing actual nilpotence by powers and rank by image-span size, matches the three histograms for m=2,3,4.
residual_risks: Own computation covers GF(2) and three block pairs only; the local-ring proof carries all prime powers and sizes. Rank data do not determine the full Jordan-partition distribution.

value.rationale: Adjacent blocks are the two-block almost-rectangular family with distinct sizes, a natural setting where the generic operator is regular but lower ranks also occur. The exact finite-field rank law measures all nongeneric ranks in that family, uniformly in q and m. This adds a useful invariant beyond a known regular-density specialization or a Jordan-type existence theorem.
residual_risks: The new contribution credited is the full ordinary-rank law, not a general Jordan-type enumeration or another regular-density result.
